duration: My whole life has been spent surrounded by immigrants, and thinking deeply on religion and its harms.
disclosure_text: Being raised with both an open family who welcomed everyone, as well as encouraged us as children to think freely, allowed me to responsibly question my environment and form a solid foundation for my future.
micronarrative: I see the misplaced anger of the protestors as rooted in a sense of shame in one’s own failings and an inability to be accountable, leading to scapegoating. This dynamic feels familiar, particularly in communities across the USA where this mentality is gaining traction. I observe people placing all their blame on migrants, claiming they are the reason for low-paying jobs or personal shortcomings. When that mentality is spoken aloud, it gives others freedom to use it as an excuse for their own inaction. If I find myself in those conversations, I am quick to speak up and stand up for what is right. My need for accountability is what is most at stake; when someone refuses to take responsibility for their own actions, I cannot proceed. This drive shapes my presence, compelling me to address the lack of ownership rather than remain silent.
